evidence.claim: Article II states that the Philippines pursues a policy of freedom from nuclear weapons in its territory and an independent foreign policy.
evidence.title: 1987 Philippine Constitution
evidence.excerpt: Article II states that the Philippines pursues a policy of freedom from nuclear weapons in its territory and an independent foreign policy.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary constitutional text; static legal baseline.
evidence.period_fit: Standing inherited constraint in 2022; not Marcos-specific.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Inherited constitutional limit on Marcos's authority, not an action by Marcos.
contrary_evidence: This establishes the baseline only; it does not show any 2022 ruler choice.

evidence.claim: SEANWFZ bars states parties from developing, possessing, stationing, transporting, testing, or using nuclear weapons, including within their territory.
evidence.title: Treaty on the Southeast Asia Nuclear Weapon-Free Zone
evidence.excerpt: SEANWFZ bars states parties from developing, possessing, stationing, transporting, testing, or using nuclear weapons, including within their territory.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary treaty text binding the Philippines and its ASEAN partners.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Inherited regional treaty constraint, not Marcos-specific conduct.
contrary_evidence: This does not show any 2022 action by Marcos; it only defines the legal environment.

evidence.claim: The Philippines has an in-force NPT safeguards agreement and an additional protocol with the IAEA.
evidence.title: Country List: Philippines
evidence.excerpt: The Philippines has an in-force NPT safeguards agreement and an additional protocol with the IAEA.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official IAEA country profile with treaty status.
evidence.period_fit: Standing safeguards status in 2022; page updated later but the agreements predate 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Inherited safeguards framework, not a 2022 Marcos decision.
contrary_evidence: The page shows peaceful-nuclear oversight, not nuclear-weapon control or crisis authority.

evidence.claim: The Philippines ratified the TPNW in February 2021, before Marcos took office.
evidence.title: The Philippines ratifies the Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons (TPNW)
evidence.publisher: United Nations Office for Disarmament Affairs
evidence.excerpt: The Philippines ratified the TPNW in February 2021, before Marcos took office.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official UN disarmament page documenting treaty ratification date.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Pre-Marcos state act; useful only as inherited baseline.
contrary_evidence: This predates Marcos and cannot be credited to his 2022 conduct.

evidence.claim: The Philippine delegation said President Marcos had told the General Assembly to reject deterrence and stay committed to decreasing the global nuclear stockpile, while warning that nuclear weapons plus emerging technologies could bring humanity closer to extinction.
evidence.title: High Level Meeting to Commemorate and Promote the International Day for the Total Elimination of Nuclear Weapons | Philippines
evidence.publisher: Permanent Mission of the Republic of the Philippines to the United Nations
evidence.excerpt: The Philippine delegation said President Marcos had told the General Assembly to reject deterrence and stay committed to decreasing the global nuclear stockpile, while warning that nuclear weapons plus emerging technologies could bring humanity closer to extinction.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Dated UN statement explicitly attributes the earlier presidential remark.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The statement explicitly attributes the deterrence line to President Marcos.
contrary_evidence: This is a public normative statement, not evidence of command-and-control or a concrete nuclear-security reform.

evidence.claim: The delegation said the Philippines' position is anchored in constitutional renunciation and a Southeast Asia nuclear-weapon-free zone, and that it had been reaffirmed by President Marcos.
evidence.title: Thematic Debate Cluster 1: Nuclear Weapons | Philippines
evidence.publisher: Permanent Mission of the Republic of the Philippines to the United Nations
evidence.excerpt: The delegation said the Philippines' position is anchored in constitutional renunciation and a Southeast Asia nuclear-weapon-free zone, and that it had been reaffirmed by President Marcos.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official UN mission statement, dated and explicitly presidentially attributed.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to the Marcos administration's public position, not to nuclear-force management.
contrary_evidence: Again, this is stance-setting, not an operational nuclear-risk intervention.

unresolved_gaps: No direct nuclear-command or crisis-use decision in 2022.
No external war or proxy-conflict record in 2022, so some conduct lenses are structurally thin.
Direct chain-of-command evidence for red-tagging and some police outcomes remains limited.
Election-year evidence is stronger on campaign behavior and information environment than on post-inauguration institutional change.
National household/distribution outcomes are better evidenced in 2023 follow-through than in clean 2022-only attribution.
Most welfare evidence is rollout or partner-supported evidence rather than a full national outcome audit.
Direct 2022 asset/SALN and office-period wealth evidence remains thin.
Agency-level execution evidence is thinner than agenda-setting and budget evidence.
